root_cause_label: Flawed Matrix Completion: NaN check on zero-filled array and unassigned SVD reconstruction
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented iterative SVD matrix completion with two fatal logic errors: it searched for missing entries using np.isnan() on a zero-filled array (missing entries are zeros, not NaN), and it computed the SVD reconstruction but never assigned it back to the working matrix, so every iteration left the matrix unchanged and the output was merely the sparse observations padded with zeros.
t_err_evidence: In step 4, the complete_matrix_svd function uses 'mask = np.isnan(dense)' to find missing entries, but sparse_matrix.toarray() fills missing entries with 0 not NaN, so mask is always all-False and the fill step is a no-op. Also, 'reconstructed = np.dot(U, np.dot(np.diag(s), Vt))' is computed but never assigned back to dense, so the SVD result is discarded every iteration.
t_commit_evidence: The broken script is written in step 4 and the same code (minus the pandas import) is used in step 6 without fixing the logic errors. Once this code is written and the pandas fix is trivial, the algorithmic failures are locked in.
t_surface_evidence: In step 7, the head output of solution_0.txt shows the matrix is mostly near-zero values (~0.001 magnitude) with sparse large values (e.g., 1.17, 1.66) matching the observed entries — exactly the pattern of zeros-padded sparse data, not a properly completed matrix. A careful reader would see the matrix is not reconstructed.
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly identified the algorithmic approach (iterative SVD matrix completion) but failed at code generation: it made two independent logic errors in the implementation — using isnan on a zero-filled array and forgetting to assign the reconstructed matrix back to the variable — demonstrating a capability limit in translating the correct algorithm into working code.
